answer: Each AI grader holds a unique quartz token forged by the network’s identity system; the token embeds a time‑varying secret drawn from nectar‑rich entropy. At random intervals a peer jury audits a tiny slice of the grader’s outputs, verifying the token’s current hash against the ledger and discarding any grade whose token fails. An attacker must create a valid quartz token for every fake identity and survive unpredictable spot‑checks, so the cost rises linearly with Sybil count, making large attacks prohibitively expensive.
